local_articles.snippet: o potentially meet in the semis. "As you say, he was in my part of the draw but it was in the semis," Alcaraz said. "For me, the semis is too far away, so I just try to be round by round." Meanwhile, Aryna Sabalenka got her bid for a third straight US Open title off to a winning start on Monday to light up the second day of the year's final Grand Slam. Former champion Iga Swiatek and last year's runner-up Amanda Anisimova also advanced with impressive victories while Stefanos Tsitsipas served up an upset by knocking out 10th seed Arthur Fils on a sunny afternoon in New York. Sabalenka looked on her way to ending a frustrating patch of poor form with a 6-2 6-4 win over Colombia's Camila Osorio that earned her a clash with Russian Polina Iatcenko in the second round. "I'm happy with my performance," said Sabalenka, who has not reached a title match since triumphing at Indian Wells and Miam

local_articles.title: US Open: Elena Rybakina brushes off injury concerns with comfortable win over Thea Frodin
local_articles.snippet: Second seed Elena Rybakina brushed off injury concerns as she began her US Open in impressive fashion, comfortably beating Thea Frodin at Flushing Meadows. The twice Grand Slam winner retired in the first set of her Cincinnati quarter-final match against Iga ​Swiatek on August 20th with an ankle problem, putting a doubt over her participation at the US Open, but she looked sharp in beating the 17-year-old American Frodin in oppressive humidity. “We’ll see how I’m going to feel tomorrow because I had to take a break [after her injury in Cincinnati]. But for now it feels okay,” Rybakina said. The Kazakhstani player could become world number one if she reaches at least the semi-finals of the US Open. “I’m definitely motivated [to get to world No 1], I had chances before but it didn’t go my way. Of course it will be an amazing achievement but it’s still too far. I need to focus on my recover

local_articles.title: Dripping in diamonds: Aryna Sabalenka’s 127-carat US Open look
local_articles.snippet: World No. 1 and defending US Open champion Aryna Sabalenka lit up Flushing Meadows with one of the most high-fashion, high-lux outfits of the 2026 tournament. Known for her bold, powerful play, Sabalenka brought serious glamor to Arthur Ashe Stadium, pairing a basketball-inspired Nike kit with over 127 carats of custom luxury jewellery. Sabalenka partnered with New York-based luxury jeweler Material Good to wear a custom jewellery collection titled “The Prism”. The suite includes a collar-style statement necklace, drop earrings, and a tennis bracelet encrusted with diamonds, sapphires, tourmalines, garnets, zircons, spinels, chrysoberyls, and tanzanites. According to the designers, the colourful mix of stones from around the world (including Cambodia, Myanmar, Tanzania, and Mozambique) was created as a tribute to the multicultural identity and vibrant energy of the “Big Apple”.

questions.title: Which film will win the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Venice Film Festival’s official announcement of its 2026 award winners. Resolution : Resolve to the film awarded the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 festival, once the winner is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning film’s title.
questions.current_reasoning: Breaking Aug 24 announcement: Venice Film Festival organizers added 'NAZA' as a late 21st title in the main Golden Lion competition—the sole documentary in the lineup. Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor (co-directors of Oscar-winning 'No Other Land') and produced/executive-produced by James Wilson and Jonathan Glazer (the exact team behind 'The Zone of Interest' and last year's Venice Grand Jury Prize runner-up 'The Voice of Hind Rajab'), 'NAZA' premieres late in the festival on Sept 10 before a jury chaired by Maggie Gyllenhaal that also includes 'Hind Rajab' director Kaouther Ben Hania, Johnnie To, and Daniel Blumberg. Because documentaries are rarely awarded Best Director, Screenplay, or Acting prizes, strong jury support concentrates directly on Golden Lion, Grand Jury Prize, and especially the Special Jury Prize (matching Venice's track record for urgent political works like 'Green Border'), vaulting 'NAZA' to #1 at 0.09 (replacing 'The Echo Chamber' in top 5). With the competition expanded to 21 films (uniform baseline 0.048) and no premieres until Sept 2, we trim Lee Chang-dong's 'Possible Love' (0.08 -> 0.07) and Werner Herzog's 'Bucking Fastard' (0.07 -> 0.06) while holding Hirokazu Kore-eda's 'Look Back' (0.07) and May el-Toukhy's 'Woman Unknown' (0.07), leaving 64% across the remaining 16 titles until screenings and reviews begin.

questions.title: Which Ukrainian city away from the eastern and southern front lines will experience repeated Russian strikes on fuel stations by September 11, 2026?
questions.background: Russian attacks have repeatedly hit fuel stations near Ukraine’s eastern and southern battle lines. The spread of this targeting pattern to cities farther from the fighting would broaden its impact on civilians.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Ukrainian municipal statements and reliable contemporaneous reporting citing local authorities. Resolution Conditions : Identify the Ukrainian city outside the eastern and southern frontline areas where Russian attacks are confirmed to have directly struck fuel stations on at least two separate days between September 1 and September 11, 2026. Reports of isolated attacks or incidental damage to nearby stations do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the city.
questions.current_reasoning: Major recalibration ahead of the Sept 1-11 window based on empirical Aug 5 NV data (200+ stations) and Aug 25 BBC deep dive (246+ stations, 114 in July alone) plus Aug 20-29 Ukrinform/UNN/DW/RBC-Ukraine reports: (1) Our prior 0.30 on Kyiv was overfit to an Aug 4 NDTV headline ('Gas Stations Across Kyiv'); NV lists Kyiv Oblast only 10th of 12 struck oblasts, zero inside-Kyiv city fuel-station strikes appeared in late-Aug reporting, and NBU noted fuel sales shifted to regions farther from front/border—cutting Kyiv 0.30 -> 0.16. (2) While Kharkiv suffered repeated strikes on Aug 20, 23-24, 28, and 29 (40% of all strikes are in Kharkiv Oblast), Kharkiv sits ~30 km from active fighting and is very likely excluded as a frontline area. (3) Dnipro (~115-150 km behind eastern/southern front lines) rises sharply 0.08 -> 0.20 as new #1: Dnipropetrovsk is the #1 oblast listed by NV alongside Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk police issued dedicated petrol-station air-raid guidance (BBC Aug 25), and stations along the Kharkiv-Dnipro road were wiped out. (4) Poltava rises 0.10 -> 0.16: unequivocally deep rear (~150+ km from front), with BBC Aug 25 confirming Russia's petrol-station campaign is actively spreading west from Kharkiv into Poltava Oblast (all stations destroyed around Opishnya). (5) Odesa holds at 0.15 (deep-rear Black Sea Shahed target with prior SOCAR fuel strikes) and Chernihiv trims 0.13 -> 0.11 (clean northern rear city on NV's struck list). Top-5 sum = 0.78, leaving 22% for Sumy (~0.07), Kryvyi Rih (~0.06), Kharkiv eligibility edge case (~0.03), Mykolaiv (~0.02), and other rear cities.

questions.title: Who will control Yemen's Mayun Island on September 11, 2026?
questions.background: Mayun, also known as Perim, is an island in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. Its location makes it strategically important for maritime traffic.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by The Associated Press or Al Jazeera identifying which military actor exercises territorial control over Mayun Island. Resolution Date : Resolve according to confirmed control on September 11, 2026. Territorial control means physical possession of the island, not merely a sovereignty claim or the ability to threaten nearby shipping. Accepted Answer Format : The commonly used name of the armed group, government, or coalition controlling the island.

With a contested amphibious seizure of fortified Mayun Island within 12 days looking increasingly remote, we trim Houthis (0.14 -> 0.09) and raise Yemeni government (0.41 -> 0.45) and Saudi-led coalition (0.20 -> 0.21), preserving spread across AP/Al Jazeera status-quo reporting labels and 5% residual.
